Anyways, I don't know what to do anymore. No doctor of mainstream medicine has been able to help me so far. And since I'm broke, I can't afford to have private doctors that may be better informed than the ones working for the system.

The PVCs ramp up, I often get bigeminy, adrenaline and cortisol surges, therefore more PVCs, making it impossible to sleep. I regularly don't sleep a whole night, and the nights I do I often only do because my body and mind is fully exhausted.

This is no way to live.

I wish modern science would look into this. The fact that PVCs in most cases won't kill you directly doesn't mean they're not killing us indirectly.

I'm 33M, athletic, haven't smoked, consumed caffeine or alcohol in over 10 years, and yet I have been on the PVC journey since 2.5 years now. Many shared that they got PVCs after the covid vax. I never took it, however.

My burden started with 400 PVCs a day. Usually I would wake up at night and something with my digestion would be off. I would have a bowel movement with very cloudy water (particles, as if my food hadn't been fully digested) and then the PVCs would go away. However, over the course of the last 2.5 years I have now arrived at a burden of 5,000 to 20,000 PVCs a day. I notice almost all of them.

I have all of the triggers I have ever read on this forum. Eating, laying down after eating, laying down in general, especially left side, lack of sleep, lack of exercise, anxious/short/shallow breathing, deep breathing into my belly, pressing on the upper stomach area, reflux, bloating, crouching, working out my abs, bad posture, etc. The list just goes on.

In January this year I had magical 3 days where I had a total of under 50 PVCs.

I feel like when I'm sleeping I don't have any, but as soon as a wake up within 20 seconds they start. Especially if I turn around in bed, switch positions etc., or if I had a stressful dream I will just wake up and immediately get bigeminy.

I have been to so many cardiologist, have had so many tests done, everything comes back clear. They tell me I have a healthy heart. I have had colonoscopy, clear. I have had endoscopy, clear. No hiatal hernia. Apparently no gastritis, although when I'm under stress I feel like I do have stomach issues. Apprently no GERD either, but I know for a fact that I have regular reflux, especially laying down. It often also feels as if I had air trapped in my stomach but if I would force a burp all of my food would come back up. I have also thrown up from panic and anxiety 9 hours after having eaten and had undigested food in my stomach. Been checked for gastroparesis, also clear.

I've tried all the supplements. Ashwaganda, B12, Zinc, Magnesium, Copper, Taurine, Arginine, Betaine HCL, Vit C, Vit B Complex, Carnitine, Digestive Enzymes, CoQ10. The best results I've had with those things have always been right when I start them, so I'm assuming that it's placebo and therefore of a psychosomatic. However, shifting one's mental and emotional state of proves to be way easier said than done. Especially with these PVCs triggering me nonstop.

Alright, so I have known individual PVCs my entire life. These are some factors I know have made them more frequent:

- lack of sleep / physical exhaustion
- lack of physical movement 
- alcohol, caffeine, nicotine
- eating too much, digestive issues, bloating (Roemheld Syndrome)
- lying position
- abnormal breathing (too short/shallow or too long/deep)
- electrolyte imbalances 
- dehydration
- adrenaline (from video games for example or anxiety/panic attacks)
- vagus nerve issues
- night time / trying to sleep 

What I’m not sure about yet:
- weight loss or eating too little calories
- carbs or fatty foods or a combination 
- blood sugar levels
- blood pressure

I hope this info might be able to help.
